evidence.note: A real type representation (types.rs) existed from the start and was later extended for vector/complex types — adapting the representation itself rather than hacking around it in codegen.

Compound-literal and bitfield support were added as coordinated changes across ast/parser/sema/codegen, showing it refactors the affected area when a feature doesn't fit the current design (level-5 behavior).
Dominant loop is per-failing-test local patching (mostly single-file codegen edits after inspecting asm), i.e. symptom-level fixes rather than diagnosing clusters as structural limitations.
Explicit 'VLA hack' in sema — chose to patch around rather than properly support, weighing against decisive redesign.

reasoning: The agent predominantly makes local, test-by-test fixes, but when features genuinely don't fit it does refactor the affected layers together (bitfields, compound literals) and even extends the type representation (types.rs) — matching the level-5 anchor of refactoring the affected area when a feature doesn't fit. It falls short of level 8 because there is no visible evidence of diagnosing clusters of failures as a shared structural cause or reasoning about redesign trade-offs, and an admitted VLA 'hack' shows tolerance for patching. Confidence is low because the trajectory exposes only tool-call descriptions, not the agent's reasoning or observations.
